'''Christiane Ayotte''', [[Order of Canada|O.C.]], is a Canadian scientist and academic from [[Quebec]]. She is currently the director of the Armand-Frappier Santé Biotechnologie Research Centre was formerly the President of the [[World Association of Anti-Doping Scientists]] from 2016{{ndash}}2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.waads.org/history |title=History |accessdate=2020-07-14 }}</ref>

==Education==
Ayotte received a [[Master of Science|MSc]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[organic chemistry]] from the [[Université de Montréal]]. Ayotte then pursued two years of post-doctoral studies in [[mass spectrometry]] at the [[Institut national de la recherche scientifique]] (INRS). 

She next became a research associate at the Doping Control Laboratory of the INRS. Since 1991, she has been director of the Doping Control Laboratory, the only Canadian laboratory accredited by the [[World Anti-Doping Agency]], and has been a research associate professor at INRS since 1992. Since 1995, she has been a member of the doping commission of the [[International Association of Athletics Federations]] and, since 1996, a member of the Working Group on Harmonization of Laboratory protocols of the [[International Olympic Committee]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.inrs.ca/english/christiane-ayotte |title=Christiane Ayotte |publisher=Institut national de la recherche scientifique}}</ref><ref name=uquebec/>

==Career==
Ayotte was named scientist of the year by [[Ici Radio-Canada Télé|Radio Canada]] in 1999.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ici.radio-canada.ca/radio/lumiere/indexscientifiques.html |title=Les scientifiques de l'année depuis 1987 |work=Les Années lumière |publisher=Radio Canada |language=fr}}</ref> In 2006, she received the [[Canadian Medical Association]]'s Medal of Honour.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.marketwired.com/press-release/christiane-ayotte-to-receive-the-cma-medal-of-honour-607599.htm |title=Christiane Ayotte to Receive the CMA Medal of Honour |date=August 11, 2006 |publisher=Canadian Medical Association}}</ref> In 2018, she was named an officer in the [[Order of Canada]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gg.ca/document.aspx?id=17122&lan=eng |title=Order of Canada Appointments |date=June 29, 2018 |publisher=Governor General of Canada}}</ref> She was also awarded a medal by the Quebec [[Ministry of International Relations (Quebec)|Ministry of International Relations and La Francophonie]] in 2018.<ref name=uquebec>{{cite web |url=http://www.uquebec.ca/reseau/fr/contenu/christiane-ayotte-recoit-un-prix-reconnaissance-du-mrif |title=Christiane Ayotte reçoit un prix reconnaissance du MRIF |publisher=University of Quebec |date=August 28, 2018 |language=fr}}</ref>

==In media==
In the 2017 documentary film ''[[Icarus (2017 film)|Icarus]]'', Ayotte can be seen berating whistleblower [[Grigory Rodchenkov]] after he came forward with allegations and details about the [[Doping in Russia|Russian doping program]].
